description: Trigger discrimination for splitting a broad goal into ordered, pull-request-sized tasks (D69, category 08 roadmap item #266) against the neighbors named in its description and the D69 scope proposal: classifying one change (change-classification-gate), writing the design (tech-spec-writer), parallel lanes versus one ordered sequence (lane-authoring-guide), writing product acceptance criteria (product-spec-writer), carrying evidence between stages (phased-work-handoff-designer), and team delivery commitments (roadmap-to-commitments-translator).

cases.prompt: Break this epic into PR-sized tasks for one agent to do in order: customers can export their invoices as CSV or PDF, filtered by date range.
cases.reason: One agent, one ordered sequence of pull-request-sized tasks from a goal too big for one change; no parallel lanes and no single change to classify.

cases.prompt: Split this effort across three parallel agents and write what each lane owns and must not touch.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (D69) — parallel lanes belong to lane-authoring-guide; an ordered sequence of PR-sized tasks belongs to ai-task-decomposer.
cases.reason: Parallel lanes with mutually exclusive boundaries and pre-work guides are lane-authoring-guide's job, not an ordered task sequence.

cases.prompt: What class is this change and what validation does it need? I'm adding a nullable column to the orders table.
cases.reason: One change that already fits one PR needs a class, validation floor and scope lock; there is nothing to split.

cases.prompt: Every time I hand the agent 'build the admin dashboard' it comes back with a 60-file diff. How should I cut the work up before handing it over?
cases.reason: The task handed to the agent is too big; the fix is an ordered plan of small tasks before work starts, not classifying one change or writing a design.

cases.prompt: Write the design doc for the new search service: architecture, data model, APIs and alternatives considered.
cases.reason: Writing the technical design is tech-spec-writer; the decomposer only splits an agreed design into tasks.

cases.prompt: Write acceptance criteria for this feature: team members can leave comments on invoices.
cases.reason: User-facing acceptance criteria for a feature belong to the product spec; the decomposer writes one done criterion per planned task, not the feature's criteria.

cases.prompt: Our migration runs in four stages across different sessions. Design how each stage hands its decisions and evidence to the next so nothing gets re-decided.
cases.reason: The stages already exist; the ask is how decisions and evidence carry between them, not how to split the work.

cases.prompt: Turn our Q3 roadmap into what the team can actually commit to, with date ranges and what we are not promising.
cases.reason: Team delivery promises from a roadmap, grounded in capacity, are roadmap-to-commitments-translator's job, not agent-sized tasks.

cases.prompt: The invoice-export story already has acceptance criteria from the product team. Tell me which of them can't be verified as written.
cases.reason: Criteria written elsewhere need a per-criterion testability review; the decomposer writes one done criterion per task it plans and does not review a story's criteria.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke reviewable-diff-discipline. My working diff for the invite API has picked up unrelated refactors; trim it back and stage only the files for the API change.
cases.reason: Keeping an in-progress diff to one intent while coding is reviewable-diff-discipline (manual-only, named here); the decomposer plans tasks before work starts and edits nothing.
